title: TableRecord
description: A structured record parsed by the Stage 3 Figure Parser from a manuscript table. Parallel to figure_record: interpretation only, no judgment, no findings produced. Previously table_records[] was referenced in SKILL.md and the report template with no contract at all (review_report.schema.json only wrote {type: object}) — promised but never defined. This file completes that contract.

table_id.description: The manuscript's original label, e.g. Table 1 / Supplementary Table S2; keep the original wording

caption.description: The table title and footnotes verbatim

scientific_question.description: What question this table is meant to answer. Judge the question first, then whether the presentation suffices to support it — the same principle as figure_record

table_kind.description: The table's purpose. baseline_characteristics and outcome_summary are the main sources for statistical forensics

columns.description: Column definitions. Denominators, units, and group membership must be made explicit here; otherwise downstream consumers cannot judge whether counts are self-consistent

group.description: Which trial arm/cohort this column belongs to; null when there is no grouping semantics

denominator.description: The denominator underlying this column's percentages. **Must be null when not explicitly written in the table; never back-derive it from row values** — a back-derived denominator produces false positives in statistical_forensics count checks

observations.description: Values extracted cell by cell. The numeric shape and provenance reuse the global definitions, consistent with figure_record.observations

footnote_definitions.description: Abbreviations, asterisk thresholds, and statistic meanings defined in the footnotes. Asterisk thresholds vary by journal; always check the footnotes instead of applying convention

parse_limitations.description: Parse limitations caused by merged cells, cross-page breaks, image-based tables, etc. **Registering one here does not mean the manuscript has a problem** — it means we could not read it, by the same logic as parse_failed != not_reported

allOf.description: When flagged for manual review, what to review must be stated — setting true without an action is as good as no hint
